1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls requireAuth, which resolves the session solely from the HttpOnly cookie and requires session.accountId to match the account, while the body parser rejects any client-supplied accountId or userId, preventing IDOR.

2.why: Verification is performed only against the single account's own encrypted TOTP secret and its stored recovery codes, so a code is bound to that account and there is no path for one user's code to authenticate another user.

3.why: The /api/mfa/verify handler sets mfaEnabled=true without invalidating or rotating any session, so the enabling session (and any other pre-existing authenticated sessions) remain fully valid after MFA is turned on.

4.why: Both the TOTP secret and the recovery-code set are stored via AES-256-GCM encrypt() (encryptedSecret, encryptedRecoveryCodes) and are only decrypted in memory when needed, never persisted in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, session IDs, CSRF tokens, TOTP seeds (randomBytes(20)), recovery codes (randomBytes(12)), and the master key are generated with node's cryptographically secure randomBytes.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, and the client keeps the CSRF token, secret, OTP, and recovery codes only in in-memory closure variables with no use of localStorage, sessionStorage, or readable cookies.

7.why: Server-side validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validCode) regex-check all inputs, the JSON body is size- and type-restricted, and the in-memory store involves no SQL, so injection via queries is not possible.

8.why: All dynamic values (secrets, codes, error messages, log lines) are inserted via textContent or createTextNode, innerHTML is used only with static templates containing no user data, and a nonce-based CSP blocks unauthorized script execution.

9.why: The application implements no redirect mechanism at all—no Location headers or redirect parameters exist and navigation is purely internal view rendering, so open redirection is impossible.

10.why: The headers() helper applies HSTS (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains), a strict nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY to every response including errors and the HTML page.

11.why: The cookie() builder sets 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=...' and clearCookie() mirrors those attributes when expiring the cookie.

12.why: The server itself performs no logging, returns only generic error messages, and the top-level catch hides stack traces, but the client-side 'Logs' panel deliberately prints the TOTP seed, the live six-digit OTP, and all recovery codes, so secrets are not kept out of log output.

13.why: TOTP codes are valid only for their 30-second window (±1 step) and the acceptedCounter check blocks reuse of the same or earlier counter, while recovery codes are spliced out upon use and carry a 30-day expiresAt that is enforced.

14.why: Both /api/mfa/verify and /api/mfa/recovery/verify call locked() and failed(), which lock the account for 10 minutes (HTTP 429) after 5 consecutive failures, with counters cleared on success.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the preauth session and issues a fresh session ID (rotation), sessions enforce a 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeout (10-minute preauth), and /api/logout deletes the server-side session and clears the cookie.
